title: fix(github-copilot): stop revoked reconnects before discovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes GitHub Copilot reconnect continuing into starter-model discovery after its caller is revoked while the saved token’s SecretRef is resolving.

## User Impact

A revoked reconnect stops before discovery. Successful reconnects, the existing confirmation, and host-authorized account selection are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow-up to 332e4d3ec02df53b18003155fe44a0a102b383e1: recheck the existing abort signal and caller authority before and after the asynchronous credential read. Keep the canonical profile selection and resolver intact.

The shared provider contract now supplies its seeded credential through the existing authorized-profile context. Registered-provider fixture setup moves unchanged into one shared test helper, allowing the new revocation regression without growing the oversized index test file.

## Evidence

On canonical main, the new revocation regression and the existing provider contract both failed for their intended reasons. After the repair, all 63 owning and sibling cases passed. Fresh full-context review through P2 found no actionable issues. The unchanged real Gateway/WebSocket replacement and revocation case also passed in 32.5 seconds on Linux/Node 24.19 (8 CPUs), with its original 90-second deadline. Provider HTTP is synthetic; this is not live GitHub authorization. The new focused regression takes 282 ms. Normal changed-file checks passed, including core/extension production and test types, scoped lint, SDK declarations, export/boundary guards, and source guards.

No UI code, prompt text, public API, credential storage, or timeout changes.
